lost_facts.assertion: probe error: Failed: no module of bespokelabs.curator.agent exports 'TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME'
lost_facts.evidence: Transcript never once contains the literal string 'TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME' (grepped, zero hits) — the agent never read the one remark that names it (g7.r1.l2, an unopened wiki comment). Despite this, from step ~66 onward the agent's own Analysis text confidently repeats 'TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME' as a settled fact 8+ times (lines 3655, 3981, 4362, 5611, 5720, 5774, 10170, 10223), apparently confabulated by pattern-matching the sibling constant TURN_LEDGER_VERSION (which IS correctly attested in the corpus, e.g. g7.r1.rev2/fix28/l10). When it actually wrote the code (full rollout JSON, msg 197/198), the constant it shipped was named `SIDECAR_FILENAME`, not `TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME` — its own stated 'settled fact' and its own code disagree.

The shipped `build_ledger()` (full rollout JSON, msg 205) takes `status: str = "verified"` as its default parameter. `processor.py`'s `_derive_ledger()` (msg 231) inherits that same bad default (`status: str = "verified"`). In `run()` (msg 237), the very first ledger derivation after writing the seed record calls `self._derive_ledger(records)` with no status argument — so it silently defaults to 'verified' instead of 'created', even though the agent's own docstrings and Analysis (e.g. line 3979: 'load_ledger = read log, rebuild in memory, verify_sidecar, nothing written') correctly describe the three-way created/adopted/verified semantics from remarks l5, l6, fix27, fix30, say20. The reasoning is right; the wiring at the one call site that matters (the fresh-run seed write) is wrong.

Same root bug as g7.r1.scope: every per-append re-derivation inside `run()`'s response loop calls `self._derive_ledger(records)` with no explicit status, which always defaults to 'verified' via the bad default parameter, overwriting whatever correct status (e.g. 'adopted', freshly computed by `load_cache()`/`verify_sidecar()` at resume) the ledger held a moment earlier. So after the sidecar is deleted and the run resumes and appends one more response, `second.ledger.status` reads 'verified' instead of the expected 'adopted'. The byte-exact JSON content (which excludes 'status') is unaffected; only the status field is wrong, and it is wrong by the same mechanism that broke g7.r1.scope.

passed_facts.quote: The three-arm verify_sidecar (absent/unreadable/old-version -> adopted; agreeing -> verified; disagreeing -> raise before anything is asked) matches the reasoning built across mail threads l9/l16/l12 and chat fix28: 'TurnLedgerDesyncError is the only raise in that module' (fix28) and the exact message format from l12's mail quote of str(exc). Shipped verify_sidecar() (msg 207) implements exactly this arm structure and the message format verbatim.

search_strategy: The agent read all delivered mail threads in bulk very early (steps 32-46, dumping/cat-ing mails 108-136 in sequence) — this is where most of r1's failure_behavior and several rule/scope clues (l3, l7, l9, l12, l16, rev1, g7r2-l05, g7r2-l08) were absorbed, effectively for free. For chat, it used a single-keyword search tool (/tmp/mm.py QUERY) against a fixed, self-chosen vocabulary — sentinel, seed, interleave_faults, next_speaker, turn_ledger, adopt, sidecar, desync, END_OF_CONVERSATION, load_ledger, sidecar_state, write_sidecar, arrow, flush, num_responses, 'turn ledger' — plus a handful of BookStack /api/search calls (ledger, 'curator agent', multi-turn/seeder/COMPLETION_SENTINEL, sidecar/verify_sidecar/TURN_LEDGER_VERSION/'agent loop'/load_ledger, END_OF_CONVERSATION). Each chat search returns only a one-line snippet per hit (`--- channel msgid timestamp` + one line), so many remarks were 'seen' as a single fragment among a pile of unrelated single lines, not as the multi-turn exchange the answer key quotes; the agent recovered full context only where it explicitly wrote/used a `mmctx.py` post-context dumper (about a dozen times) or did a wholesale channel/page dump. This keyword-driven strategy is why chat channels never independently searched for (#cookbooks got exactly one incidental visit via a 'ledger' hit; #viewer, #releases, #incidents were each visited once or not at all) and remarks worded without any of the chosen keywords (negotiation demo, subclassed, typed it lowercase, full stop) were never found even though they carry graded facts. Crucially, the agent NEVER opened, searched for, or listed docs/meetings/weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-2-release-ci.md at any point — a real, searchable BookStack page (confirmed by grep: zero hits for 'weekly-sync'/'release-ci'/'jun-2') — losing all three remarks planted there (l2, g7r2-l04, g7r2-l10) including the only literal statement of TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME in the whole corpus. Wiki comments were fetched properly once the agent debugged its page-dumping script (step 63-64) to surface comments.active[].comment.html, and from then on it systematically pulled comments off pages 139/143/144/150/152/147, recovering essentially all of the comment-carried clues it discovered the pages for.
end_reason: Run completed normally: merged to main (commit f92da98), CI green, deployed and health-checked (line 10223). reward=0.625 reflects 5/8 hidden facts (g7.open_feature is weight-0); all four g7.r2 facts and one of four g7.r1 facts (failure_behavior) scored 1. The three lost g7.r1 facts (rule/scope/observability) are NOT information-recovery failures — the agent's own Analysis text correctly recovered the created/adopted/verified three-status design and (independently, via confabulation) the TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME name — they are implementation bugs in the shipped code: a wrong constant name (SIDECAR_FILENAME vs the claimed TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME) and a bad default parameter (`status: str = "verified"`) that silently overwrites the correct created/adopted status at every call site that matters.
notable: The agent initially DISMISSED the entire r1 sidecar/ledger thread as belonging to 'a neighbouring system (the executor), not our module' (line 2188, step 33) while reading mail — it only recovered by continuing to read broadly and later (step 41+) correctly tying it back to the ticket's own module.

TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME is never once present in the transcript, yet the agent states it as a settled corpus fact 8+ times from step 66 onward (lines 3655, 3981, 4362, 5611, 5720, 5774, 10170, 10223) — an apparent confabulation from the sibling constant TURN_LEDGER_VERSION's naming pattern, then shipped under yet a THIRD name, SIDECAR_FILENAME, in the actual code (rollout JSON msg 198) — three different names (never-seen TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME claimed as fact, then SIDECAR_FILENAME shipped) for what the one corpus page (never opened) calls TURN_LEDGER_FILENAME.

docs/meetings/weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-2-release-ci.md — a real, BookStack-searchable page carrying 3 remarks (g7.r1.l2, g7.r2.g7r2-l04, g7.r2.g7r2-l10) across both requirements and all three surface types (body + 2 comments) — was never touched by any tool call in the entire 183-step run.

#cookbooks was visited exactly once (line 3126, step 50, via an incidental 'ledger' keyword hit landing on a Dec-29 message), even though 5 of the corpus's remarks live there (g7r2-l01, g7r2-l06, say25, plus both r2 herrings partially); this is the least-covered channel.

The build_ledger()/`_derive_ledger()` default `status: str = "verified"` is a single-line implementation bug that alone accounts for both lost g7.r1.scope and g7.r1.observability facts — the run() loop never passes an explicit status at the two call sites where 'created' or the load-derived status should be preserved.
